second_order: Building, fixing, and defending the logo
theme_note: Hands-on canvas practice joins target-setting, placing, repair calls, alarms, relocation, and repeated defense; what varies is the mark, its scale, and whether work is prospective, active, or restorative.

second_order: Coordinating through Discord, scripts, and shared plans
theme_note: Builders make labour reproducible and reachable through Discord rooms, invitations, reference grids, overlays, scripts, alternate accounts, and divisions of maintenance; views on automation vary inside the practice.

second_order: Making deals and sharing space with neighbours
theme_note: Participants bargain over borders, overlap, reciprocal defense, incorporated art, and shared targets with neighbouring groups; outcomes range from refusal through provisional truce to reported alliance.

second_order: Moving Place talk out of the main room
theme_note: Members and moderators try to contain the flood of Place posts through locks, filtering, a sticky, and repeated redirection to r/osuplace; compliance, fatigue, and exceptions vary.

second_order: Turning April Fools into subreddit play
theme_note: The room deliberately bends subreddit identity, university language, score formats, announcements, and familiar game conventions into April Fools performances, while other participants decode, resist, or end the joke.

second_order: Celebrating and preserving the Great Defense
theme_note: Participants turn live milestones and the ending into communal achievement through thanks, pride, timelapses, histories, archives, memes, banners, and news reactions; celebration is also qualified by loss and criticism.

second_order: Arguing over size, scripts, and whose art counted
theme_note: Participants contest whether the logo is too large, automated, unfair, destructive of other art, or entitled to remain; defenses, apologies, concessions, and accusations vary within the same evaluative practice.

second_order: Raiding, retaliating, and arguing over blame
theme_note: Raid slogans, hostile incursions, counter-raids, clips, and later explanations all act on the conflict and allocate responsibility; positions range from taunting to retaliation to qualified forgiveness.

second_order: Turning pixel work into osu! jokes and welcoming newcomers
theme_note: Participants recast pixels in osu! language and use the visible defense as an entry into the game, welcoming newcomers with maps, songs, help, and local jokes.

second_order: Trying to keep the logo going after Place
theme_note: After the official canvas closes, small groups try to rebuild on replacement canvases; enthusiasm ranges from immediate recruitment to rapid dismissal and weak uptake.
